title: Hotel Rates
intro: Hotel Rates holds every hotel's rate plans. A quotation uses only **approved** published rates. Drafts are never used for a price.

guide.title: Hotel Rates step by step, A to Z
guide.intro: The hotel sends a rate sheet, the Hotel Desk puts it into the system as a draft, a manager checks and approves it, and then the inquiry can use the price.

stages.title: Stage 1 — Put the hotel's rates into the system

steps.title: Open Hotel Rates
steps.text: Go to **Master Files → Hotel Rates (new)** (on the Tour Desk bar: **Hotel Rates**, or **Masters → Hotel Rates**). (1) the toolbar, (2) the red **RATE EXPIRY WARNING** box, (3) **Add rates**, (4) the search box.

steps.title: Find the hotel
steps.text: Type part of the hotel name in **Search hotel, location, chain or code** (1) and click the hotel (2). Green **rate today** = the hotel has an approved price for today.

steps.title: Look at what the hotel already has
steps.text: The top of the hotel page shows today's price and **Watch out** (extra charges such as gala dinners). Scroll to **Published rates**: look at **Markets** (who the plan is for; empty = all markets) and **Status** (*draft*, *approved*, *superseded*). If the new sheet is already here as a draft, do not read it again — go to Stage 2.

steps.title: Open Read a PDF
steps.text: Click **Add rates** (1), then **Read a PDF** (2).

steps.title: Choose the PDF and press Preview
steps.text: (1) Under **Contract PDF / image** click **Choose file**, pick the PDF, then **Read**. (2) Check **Defaults for this file**: Hotel, Plan type *Contract*, Markets (empty = all), Pricing *Per room*, Currency. (3) Click **Preview**. Nothing is saved yet.

steps.title: Check the preview, then Save as drafts
steps.text: Compare the preview with the PDF: the right hotel, **one plan per market table**, every date band, the prices. This example is wrong — four market tables became one *All markets* plan — so the right action is **Close** and ask a manager. When the preview is right, tick **I have read the warnings** and click **Save as drafts**.

stages.title: Stage 2 — Check and approve the rates
stages.who: A manager with the Hotel Rate Approval permission

steps.title: Open the draft and compare it with the PDF
steps.text: On **Published rates**, click **Edit** on the draft (or **Open** in the **Approval queue**). (1) plan name and status, (2) the sections menu, (3) **Markets** — the purple ones are included.

steps.title: Check Seasons & rates
steps.text: (1) the season name is only a label, (2) the **dates** decide the price and must match the PDF, (3) room type, meal plan and SGL / DBL / TPL must match the PDF.

steps.title: Read the Checks
steps.text: **Checks** shows errors (they stop approval) and warnings (read each one). A warning is fine when the PDF really says so.

steps.title: Approve
steps.text: Click the green **Approve** on the draft's row. If **Warnings to confirm** opens, read it and click **Approve anyway** only if the sheet says so. If nothing seems to happen, look for that box.

steps.title: Or approve from the Approval queue
steps.text: The **Approval queue** lists every draft from every hotel. (1) **Checks** shows *clean* or the number of warnings, (2) **Open** to check, then **Approve**.

steps.title: Retire old or duplicate plans
steps.text: Open **More** on the extra plan: (1) **Correct the approved plan** to fix it in place, (2) **Mark as superseded** to retire an old or duplicate copy. Keep the plan that inquiries already use.

stages.title: Stage 3 — Use the rates on the inquiry

steps.title: Open the inquiry
steps.text: Go to **Tour Inquiry**, find the inquiry and click **Open** (2). (1) **Nothing outstanding** = every night is priced; (3) **1 hotel unpriceable** = a night still has no approved rate.

steps.title: Click Check hotels again
steps.text: At the bottom of the inquiry, in the row with **Back to list**, click **Check hotels again**. Nights with no price take the newest approved rate; nights with a price keep it. It does not confirm the tour.

steps.title: If asked, choose the room type
steps.text: If a night shows **Choose room type**, click it (or **Edit**). In the **Night** window pick (1) the **Room type** — normally *(the hotel's normal type)* — and check (2) the meal plan, then **Save**.

steps.title: Check every night shows Published rate
steps.text: Each night should show a green **Published rate** with the room type and price.

steps.title: Morning check (5 minutes)
steps.text: Open **Hotel Rates (new)**. Red **RATE EXPIRY WARNING**: e-mail those hotels for new rates. **Approval queue** count: ask the manager to check the drafts. **Health check**: tours with a night without a rate. **Hotel Incomplete Work**: anything else missing.

topics.title: Approve hotel rates
questions: Where do I go to approve hotel rates?
How do I approve a rate plan?
Where is the approval queue?
How do I sign off a hotel rate sheet?
Approve the rates a colleague uploaded
topics.audience: Managers with the Hotel Rate Approval permission
topics.needs_note: Approving needs the **Hotel Rate Approval** permission. Ask a person who has it to approve, and tell them the hotel name and which plan.
topics.summary: Approve in **Hotel Rate Approval**: it opens Hotel Rates with the **Approval queue** — every draft from every hotel. Check each draft against the hotel's sheet, then click **Approve**.

steps.text: Open **Master Files → Hotel Rate Approval**. (Already in **Hotel Rates (new)**? Click **Approval queue** in the toolbar.)
The **Approval queue** lists every draft. **Checks** shows *clean* or the number of warnings.
Click **Open** on a draft. Compare it with the hotel's PDF: **Markets**, every season's **dates** and the **SGL / DBL / TPL** prices.
When everything matches, click **Approve**.
If **Warnings to confirm** opens, read each line and click **Approve anyway** only if the sheet really says so. If **Cannot approve yet** opens, fix the line it names first.
Open each inquiry that uses this hotel and click **Check hotels again**. Inquiries do not update by themselves.

notes: Opening the queue approves nothing. Only the **Approve** button does.
Approving makes the price live for new quotations straight away.

images.caption: The Approval queue: (1) Checks, (2) Open and Approve

topics.title: Upload a hotel rate sheet (PDF)
questions: How do I upload a hotel rate sheet?
How do I read a PDF rate sheet into the system?
Where do I add a new hotel contract?
The hotel sent new rates, how do I put them in?
topics.needs_note: Reading a rate sheet needs the **Hotel Rates (new)** permission. Ask the Hotel Desk to do it, or ask the System Administrator for access.
topics.summary: In **Hotel Rates (new)** use **Add rates → Read a PDF**. The system reads the sheet into a **draft**; you check the preview and click **Save as drafts**. A manager approves it later.

steps.text: Open **Master Files → Hotel Rates (new)** (Tour Desk bar: **Hotel Rates**).
Search for the hotel and click it. On **Published rates**, check the sheet is not already there as a draft. If it is, do not read it again — check that draft instead.
Click **Add rates → Read a PDF**.
Under **Contract PDF / image** click **Choose file**, pick the PDF, then click **Read** and wait.
Check **Defaults for this file**: **Hotel**, **Plan type** (*Contract*), **Markets** (empty = all markets), **Pricing** (*Per room*), **Currency**.
Click **Preview** and compare it with the PDF: the right hotel, **one plan per market table**, every date band, the prices.
Tick **I have read the warnings** and click **Save as drafts**.

notes: Saving the same sheet twice makes a duplicate plan.
If the preview shows one *All markets* plan for a sheet with separate market tables, click **Close** and ask a manager.
**Save & approve** is shown only to people with Hotel Rate Approval. Use it only after checking every figure.

topics.title: Import an Excel rate sheet
questions: How do I import rates from Excel?
Can I upload an Excel file of hotel rates?
Where is the Excel template for hotel rates?
topics.summary: Use **Add rates → Import an Excel sheet**. Three layouts are understood: the workbook from **Download template**, a long list, or the old wide upload.

steps.text: Open **Hotel Rates (new)**.
Click **Add rates → Import an Excel sheet** (or on the hotel: **New plan → Import from Excel…**).
Under **Excel file** click **Choose file** and pick the workbook. To start from a clean layout, use **Download template** first.
Set **Defaults for this file** and click **Preview**.
Compare the preview with the hotel's sheet, tick **I have read the warnings**, then click **Save as drafts**.

notes: Blank cells mean *not offered*. Never type 0.

topics.title: Check a draft before it is approved
questions: How do I check a draft rate plan?
How do I review rates before approving?
What should I compare before approving?
topics.needs_note: Opening a plan needs the **Hotel Rates (new)** permission.
topics.summary: Open the draft and go through its sections with the hotel's PDF beside you. Fix anything wrong and click **Save draft**.

steps.text: Open **Hotel Rates (new)** and click the hotel.
On **Published rates**, click **Edit** on the draft. (In the **Approval queue** it is **Open**.)
**Overview**: name, stay dates (**Valid from / to**), **Markets** — the purple ones are included.
**Seasons & rates**: every season's **dates** and every **SGL / DBL / TPL** price must match the PDF. The season name is only a label.
**Checks**: errors must be fixed; warnings must be read.
If you changed anything, click **Save draft**. Then a manager approves it.

notes: Dates decide which rate a night gets — not the season name.

topics.title: Enter hotel rates by hand
questions: How do I enter rates manually?
How do I type in a rate plan without a PDF?
How do I create a new rate plan?
Add a new contract by hand
topics.needs_note: Entering rates needs the **Hotel Rates (new)** permission.
topics.summary: Open the hotel and use **New plan → Contract (season rates)**. Fill **Overview**, then **Seasons & rates**, then **Save draft**.

steps.text: Open **Hotel Rates (new)** and click the hotel.
Click **New plan → Contract (season rates)**.
**Overview**: plan name, **Valid from (stay)** and **Valid to (stay)**, **Markets** (none selected = all), currency and pricing.

**Seasons & rates**: season name and dates (**+ date range** for a second period). Add rows with **+ row** or **Fill grid**, or **Paste** cells copied from Excel. Type SGL / DBL / TPL exactly as printed.
Fill other sections the sheet covers: **Room supplements & meal deltas**, **Supplements & meals**, **Children & extra beds**, **Cancellation & payment**.
Click **Check**, fix any errors, then **Save draft**. A manager approves it.

notes: Enter each market table of a sheet as its own plan, with its markets set on **Overview**.

topics.title: Correct a wrong hotel rate
questions: How do I correct a rate?
How do I fix a wrong price on an approved plan?
How do I change a hotel rate?
I entered the wrong rate, how do I edit it?
topics.needs_note: Changing rates needs the **Hotel Rates (new)** permission.
topics.summary: A **draft**: open it with **Edit**, fix it, **Save draft**. An **approved** plan: **More → Correct the approved plan**, fix it, **Save correction**. Never delete or retype a second copy.

steps.text: Open **Hotel Rates (new)**, click the hotel and find the plan on **Published rates**.
If the plan is a **draft**: click **Edit**, fix the figure, click **Save draft**.
If the plan is **approved**: click **More → Correct the approved plan**, fix the figure, click **Save correction**. The fix applies at once.
Inquiries that already copied the old figure show **Rate changed in Hotel Rates**. Click **Use the new rate** on a night only if the new price should apply to that tour.

notes: Correcting keeps the plan's history. Use **More → Who changed it** to see it.

images.caption: More menu: (1) Correct the approved plan, (2) Mark as superseded

topics.title: Same sheet uploaded twice (duplicate plans)
questions: I uploaded the same rate sheet twice
How do I remove a duplicate rate plan?
How do I retire an old rate plan?
How do I delete a draft?
topics.needs_note: Working with plans needs the **Hotel Rates (new)** permission.
topics.summary: Keep the plan that inquiries already use. An extra **draft**: **More → Delete draft**. An extra **approved** plan: **More → Mark as superseded**. Never delete an approved plan.

steps.text: Open **Hotel Rates (new)** and click the hotel.
On **Published rates**, compare the two plans: name, source file, stay dates, **Markets**, **Status**.
Find the one inquiries use: the inquiry night shows the plan name. Keep that one.
If the extra copy is a **draft**: **More → Delete draft**.
If the extra copy is **approved**: **More → Mark as superseded** and confirm **Supersede**.

notes: A superseded plan stays in history and no longer prices new nights.
A new sheet for dates already covered: approve the new plan, then **Mark as superseded** on the old one.

topics.title: Why is a hotel rate not appearing in my inquiry?
questions: Why is the hotel rate not showing in the inquiry?
The inquiry shows no rate for a hotel
I approved the rate but the inquiry still has no price
Why does it say published rate missing?
Hotel unpriceable on my inquiry
topics.needs_note: Opening inquiries needs the **Tour Inquiry** permission.
topics.summary: Read the message on the night — it says why. Most often the rate was approved after the inquiry was checked (click **Check hotels again**), a draft is still waiting for approval, or the approved plan is for another market.

steps.text: Open the inquiry (**Tour Inquiry → Open**) and read the message on the hotel night.
If the rate was approved recently: click **Check hotels again** at the bottom of the inquiry.
*… draft plan(s) cover … but are not approved yet*: a manager must check and approve the right draft in **Hotel Rate Approval**.
*No approved plan covers …*: there is no approved rate for those dates. The Hotel Desk reads the hotel's new sheet; a manager approves it.
*… covers … but not for market JP* (or another market): the approved plan is for other clients. Approve the plan whose **Markets** include the client's market.
*… has no season dated for it*: the dates fall in a gap. Add the season in the plan.
*Only … (tactical offer) covers …*: offers are never quoted. Enter the hotel's contract for those dates.
**Choose room type** on the night: click it and pick the room.

notes: To see which plan prices each night: **Hotel Rates (new)** → the hotel → **Coverage** tab, choose the **Market**.
A night that already has a figure keeps it. If Hotel Rates changed later, the night shows **Rate changed in Hotel Rates** with **Use the new rate**.

images.caption: Check hotels again, at the bottom of the inquiry

has: has no season dated for it
never an offer or tactical rate

topics.title: Update an inquiry with newly approved rates (Check hotels again)
questions: Where is Check hotels again?
How do I refresh the hotel rates on an inquiry?
The new rate is approved, how do I get it into the inquiry?
topics.needs_note: Opening inquiries needs the **Tour Inquiry** permission.
topics.summary: Open the inquiry and click **Check hotels again** at the bottom, in the row with **Back to list**.

steps.text: Go to **Tour Inquiry** and click **Open** on the inquiry.
Scroll to the bottom. Under the status buttons (**Mark as quoted**, **Confirm Tour** …) click **Check hotels again**.
Look at each hotel night: it should show a green **Published rate**.

notes: Nights with no price take the newest approved rate; nights with a price keep it.
It does not confirm the tour or change its status.

topics.title: Choose the room type on an inquiry night
questions: The inquiry says choose room type
How do I change the room type on a night?
Which room type should I pick?
topics.needs_note: Opening inquiries needs the **Tour Inquiry** permission.
topics.summary: Click **Choose room type** (or **Edit**) on the night, pick the **Room type** in the **Night** window, then **Save**.

steps.text: Open the inquiry.
On the night, click **Choose room type** (or **Edit**).
In the **Night** window choose **Room type** — normally the one marked *(the hotel's normal type)*. Check the **Meal plan**.
Click **Save**. To only look, click **Cancel**.

notes: Two names for the same room in Hotel Rates (for example *Standard* and *Standard Room*) make the inquiry ask. Tidy them on the hotel's **Room types** tab.

topics.title: Markets: which clients a rate plan is for
questions: Why is the rate not used for a Japanese client?
How do markets work on rate plans?
Which plan prices a night?
topics.needs_note: Viewing plans needs the **Hotel Rates (new)** permission.
topics.summary: A plan prices a night only for the markets it includes. No market selected = all markets. The inquiry's market comes from the agent's country (Japan → JP).

steps.text: Open **Hotel Rates (new)** and click the hotel.
On **Published rates**, read the **Markets · tier** column of each approved plan.
Open the **Coverage** tab and choose the **Market** to see **Which plan prices each night**.
If no approved plan includes the client's market, approve the plan for that market (for example the Asia plan that includes JP).

notes: On a plan's **Overview**, click a market once to include it, twice to exclude it, a third time to clear.

topics.title: The hotel has not sent new rates (use last year's)
questions: The hotel has not sent new rates yet
How do I copy last year's rates to next year?
Use the same rates for next season
topics.needs_note: Copying a plan needs the **Hotel Rates (new)** permission; approving it needs **Hotel Rate Approval**.
topics.summary: First ask the hotel. If a manager decides to keep last year's prices, use **More → Copy for next year (+1 year)** on last season's plan, check it and approve it. Replace it when the hotel's sheet arrives.

steps.text: Ask the hotel for the new rate sheet. Using old prices is a manager's decision.
Open the hotel. On last season's plan click **More → Copy for next year (+1 year)**. A new draft opens with every date one year later and the same prices.
Put *carried forward* in the plan name, check the dates, click **Save draft**.
A manager approves it.
When the hotel's sheet arrives, read it in, approve it and **Mark as superseded** on the carried-forward plan.

topics.title: Room types of a hotel
questions: How do I add a room type to a hotel?
The same room has two names
How do I set a suite as base plus supplement?
topics.needs_note: Editing room types needs the **Hotel Rates (new)** permission.
topics.summary: Open the hotel → **Room types** tab. Add a room with **Add a room type**. Keep one name per room.

steps.text: Open **Hotel Rates (new)** and click the hotel.
Open the **Room types** tab.
To add a room: type its name in **Add a room type** exactly as the hotel writes it, click **Add**.
**Priced as**: *base rate* when the sheet prints its own prices, *base + suppl.* when it is another room plus a supplement.
Two names for the same room: use one name in every plan and set the other row's **Status** to *inactive*.

topics.title: See a hotel's price for a date
questions: How do I see the price of a hotel for a date?
How much is the hotel on a certain night?
Where is try a quote?
topics.needs_note: Viewing rates needs the **Hotel Rates (new)** permission. Without it, ask the Hotel Desk.
topics.summary: Open the hotel: the **Rate on** card at the top shows every room and meal for a date. Change the date, **Nights** and **Market**. For a whole stay use **Try a quote**.

steps.text: Open **Hotel Rates (new)** and click the hotel.
In the **Rate on** card set the date, **Nights**, **Market** and **Rooms**.
Read the table (SGL / DBL / TPL for each room and meal) and **Watch out** (gala dinners, peak charges, minimum stays).
For a stay priced night by night, click **Try a quote** in the toolbar.

topics.title: Approve does nothing / warnings and errors
questions: I clicked approve and nothing happened
What does Warnings to confirm mean?
It says cannot approve yet
What is warning W09?
topics.needs_note: Approving needs the **Hotel Rate Approval** permission. Ask a person who has it.
topics.summary: **Warnings to confirm**: read each warning; click **Approve anyway** only if the hotel's sheet really says so. **Cannot approve yet**: an error must be fixed first.

steps.text: Look for a pop-up box after clicking **Approve** — the plan is not approved until you answer it.
**Warnings to confirm** (amber, codes W…): for example W09 = prices changed a lot against the latest approved plan. If the PDF says so, click **Approve anyway**.
**Cannot approve yet** (red, codes E…): open the plan with **Edit**, go to **Checks**, click the line to jump to it, fix it, **Save draft**, then approve again.

images.caption: Checks: errors stop approval, warnings must be read

topics.title: Rate expiry warning and the morning check
questions: What is the rate expiry warning?
Which hotels' rates are ending soon?
What should I check every morning in hotel rates?
topics.summary: The red **RATE EXPIRY WARNING** box lists hotels whose approved rate ends within the warning period with nothing approved after it. Ask those hotels for new rates.

steps.text: Open **Hotel Rates (new)** and read the red **RATE EXPIRY WARNING** box.
E-mail each hotel listed for its new rate sheet. **Open quotation readiness** shows the detail.
Check the **Approval queue** count and ask the manager to clear it.
Click **Health check** for tours with a night without a rate, and open **Hotel Incomplete Work** for anything else missing.

notes: The warning clears by itself when an approved rate covers the night after.
topics.manual_ref: Hotel Rates → Step by step, Stage 4 (step 17)

topics.title: Who can upload, approve or correct hotel rates?
questions: Who can approve hotel rates?
Why can't I see the Approve button?
What permission do I need for hotel rates?
topics.summary: Three permissions (menu entries) control Hotel Rates. People without **Hotel Rate Approval** do not see the **Approve** buttons. The System Administrator has all three. Permissions are set under **Settings → Group Privileges**; log out and in again after a change.

steps.text: **Hotel Rates (new)**: open the screen, read PDFs and Excel **as drafts**, edit drafts, delete drafts, copy plans, room types, hotel details.
**Hotel Rate Approval**: **Approve**, **Save & approve**, **Correct the approved plan**, **Mark as superseded**, merge duplicate hotels, Settings.
**Hotel Incomplete Work**: the list of what is missing.
Your own access is shown at the top of every answer in this manual.

topics.title: The old Hotel Rate screen is locked
questions: Why can't I edit rates in the old Hotel Rate screen?
The old hotel rate page is locked
topics.needs_note: Use **Hotel Rates (new)**; ask the Hotel Desk if you do not have it.
topics.summary: The old **Hotel Rate** screen is only for looking. Rates are entered and approved in **Hotel Rates (new)**; the old rows are rebuilt from approved plans automatically.

steps.text: Open **Master Files → Hotel Rates (new)** instead.
